## Zone 1 — Rulings and scope (binding)

- Type **Bug**. The defect: a panel authored without `childObject` asks the backend to `find` an object literally named `undefined`, scoped by `{ [relationshipField]: parentId }`.
- **The design sub-question is in scope for you**, and triage set the default: *"following #5940's config-hint precedent is the default, deviation is a report-not-assume."*
- ⛔ The pin is **not** to be deleted or weakened — it is to be **flipped**, per its own comment, and its annotation removed. It is the card's acceptance evidence.

## The judgement this card exists for — read the card's own paragraph before coding

Unlike #6188's, this decline is **not purely mechanical**, and the card says exactly why: declining a *schema* fetch has no visible consequence (the panel already holds `null`), but `load` **owns `loading`**, and the render branches `loading ? "Loading…" : !parentId ? "Save the record first…" : `. So a panel that declines with a `parentId` bound falls to the third branch and shows **an empty editable grid with an Add button, over an object that does not exist**.

⭐ That is a worse user-facing outcome than the bug you are fixing, and it is reachable *because* of your fix. #5940's config-hint card is the precedent and the default. Whichever branch you land on, the report must say which and why — ⛔ do not let `loading` stay true forever as a way of hiding the state, and ⛔ do not leave the empty-grid branch unconsidered.

## Zone 2 — Not verified by the card, and worth your measurement

The card explicitly leaves one thing unmeasured: whether the same shape exists on the **save path** — `buildMasterDetailEditBatch` is handed `childObject: schema.childObject` unconditionally (card cites `:205`; I read `:227` today). Its reasoning is that Save is disabled until the grid is dirty, so reaching it needs editing rows of a nonexistent object first — *"plausible but not measured"*.

⛔ Do not widen into a save-path fix on a guess. **Measure it**: if reachable, say so and file it (or fold it only if it is the same one-line guard on the same code path — argue it). If unreachable, say what makes it unreachable. Either way the card's open question closes with a reading instead of staying open.

## Zone 3 — Suggested route (optional; measurement wins)

Guard `load` the way `:129` guards the schema fetch — same shape, same voice in the console message — and give the unresolvable case its own render branch following #5940 rather than letting it land on the editable-grid branch. ⛔ My guess; if the code reads better another way, take it and say why.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. `packages/plugin-form` is a released package, so follow `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s own verdict; ⛔ no `skip-changeset` label (#4912). The flipped pin **is** your red-before/green-after evidence — show it failing against the old expectation and passing against the new one. Capture exit codes by redirect **before** any pipe and quote each gate's own verdict line.

⛔ Do not edit `content/docs/releases/`.

## Standing

Worktree-first before your first edit. Post **your own claim comment** with your branch — ⚠️ under `mode:subagent` your session ID is identical to mine (objectstack#12220), so the branch is what distinguishes it. Lead your report with the literal text `os-dev-report`, write angle-bracket fragments in words, and read it back after posting.

Expected outcome: `done` with a draft PR carrying `Fixes #6194`.

## ACCEPT — PR #6359

`domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R30. Read against the diff and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report.

### ⭐ The open question closed with a measurement, and the card's hedge was too generous

The card left the save path *"plausible but not measured"*, reasoning that reaching it needs *"editing rows of the nonexistent object first"*. Measured on the **pre-fix** component:

```
grid rendered        = true
Add button           = true
Save disabled at t0  = true
after ONE keystroke in the always-present ghost row:
Save disabled        = false
reached the adapter  = batchTransaction([{ object: undefined, action: 'create',
                                           data: { qty: 3, invoice: 'inv-1' } }])
```

⭐ **One keystroke, and it reaches a WRITE** — through the very affordance the empty grid advertises (*"No items yet — click Add to begin"*), without the Add button being touched at all. The bad read was one keystroke from a bad write, and the card's own framing understated it.

**Folding the save guard was the right call and it met my stated condition** — *"fold it only if it is the same one-line guard on the same code path, argue it."* It is one token added to the existing `if (!dataSource || !parentId) return;` at the component's other data-layer entry point: same defect class, same gate family, no new verification surface. And the argument for why the guard is still needed once the grid is gone is the good part: the render branch removes the only producer of `dirty`, but *"a write contract is not the render tree's to keep"* — the guard covers the one route rendering cannot close, a schema edited to drop `childObject` while rows are already dirty. **The third new test exercises exactly that route**, and asserts the precondition (Save actually enabled) rather than assuming it — without which the test would pass for a Save that was disabled the whole time and prove nothing.

### ⭐ It followed the precedent's SHAPE and refused its COPY — because it measured the precedent

Triage's default was *"follow #5940's config-hint precedent"*. The dev followed the shape and deliberately not the copy, because it measured that **#5940's config hint does not exist**. I verified that myself on `origin/main`:

- `MasterDetailForm.tsx:243` renders exactly one thing for an unresolved detail — `Loading columns…`
- its own comments at `:351` and `:382` twice promise *"the grid card shows a config hint"*
- `childObject` appears in **no rendered branch** of that file — only in a `key=`, a type, comments and a `console.warn`

So the precedent named in the order is a **spinner that can never stop being wrong, and never names the key**. Copying it would have reproduced, in the card that ruled it out by name, the outcome the card ruled out. Filed as **#6360** (labelled `finding`), and it is arguably the more valuable half of this delivery.

The landed branch is checked **ahead of `loading`**, with the reason stated: *"nothing here is pending — the schema itself already says this panel can never resolve, so there is no first paint where Loading… is true."* ⛔ `loading` is never held true to hide the state, which was my explicit prohibition.

### The pin, flipped not weakened

`expect(calls).toEqual(['find(undefined)'])` → `toEqual([])`, annotation removed, **exact-list shape kept** — with the reason preserved in the file: an exact list is the only shape that catches *a third* unguarded read of this key being added, which is how the second one arrived. Shown red before (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'find(undefined)' ]`) and green after.

⭐ One detail in the test harness worth keeping: the write channel spells ops with `String(op.object)` rather than `JSON.stringify`, because **`JSON.stringify` drops an undefined value** — so the op for an unresolvable panel would have read as a create carrying no object key at all, rather than one naming `undefined`. An instrument that would have hidden the very thing it was built to catch.

Both declines now say **which** read they refused (`refusing to fetch its child schema` / `refusing to fetch its rows`), asserted separately so a failure names which half broke.

### Checklist

| Criterion | Reading |
|:--|:--|
| Diff | 3 files — component, its test, a changeset |
| Changeset | gate went red first (`2 source file(s) … adds no changeset`), then a **real patch** changeset, ⛔ not empty frontmatter — correct, the behaviour change is user-visible |
| Governed surface | clean |
| CI | 27 checks, zero failures so far, shards still running |

Not-measured gates reported **as prerequisites rather than passes or failures**: `check-readme-exports` (needs a build), `check-eager-closure-budget` (exit 2, self-declares "a broken gauge, not a passing budget"), `check-half-states` (exit 3, self-declares "it is no reading at all"). None implicated by this diff.

⭐ **And a gate-derivation trap worth recording lane-wide**: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` lives only in objectstack and answers only about the tree it sits in — feeding it objectui paths would have produced objectstack's gate families, *"complete in shape, exit 0, entirely wrong."* The list was derived by hand from objectui's own `package.json` and its 28 workflows instead. That is a confidently-wrong answer avoided by noticing which repo a tool belongs to.

### Landing

Arming on every-check-green — ⛔ not the required subset. Your channel deviation (REST 403 from the dev seat, dedup via MCP `search_issues` plus a local grep) is noted and was the right call to flag rather than take silently; #6358 records the same limitation from the #6264 dev.

⚠️ The sanitizer stripped the angle-bracket fragment naming the grid element from the card body **and from my dispatch order** — so my own quote of the render branch was missing its third arm. Third sanitizer casualty this round; it is on the platform-fact card objectstack#12200's family.
